stories.title: Accenture rolls out performance bonuses
stories.summary: Accenture has begun its November 2026 bonus cycle, with payouts ranging from 0 percent to 27 percent globally. In India, where the firm employs roughly half of its 8.14 lakh staff, bonuses are capped at 26 percent. Non-performers received nothing. The system rewards performance with variable percentages.

stories.title: Accenture India rolls out bonuses of up to 26%, salary hikes largely on hold - Moneycontrol.com
Accenture Rolls Out Up To 26% Performance Bonus For Top Employees, Salary Hikes Remain On Hold - News18
Accenture offers bonuses up to 26%, freezes most salary hikes - NewsBytes
Accenture freezes salary hikes despite bonus payouts
stories.summary: Accenture is offering performance-based bonuses of up to 26 percent to top-performing employees in India as part of its November 2026 cycle. While bonuses are moving, annual salary increases remain largely frozen and promotions are restricted. Performance ratings now determine the size of the reward.

stories.title: Accenture increases bonus range for top performers
stories.summary: Accenture is rolling out performance-linked bonuses of up to 27 percent for eligible global employees, with Indian staff receiving between 8 percent and 26 percent. This year's range exceeds the previous year's 5 percent to 15 percent. Non-performers receive no bonus at all.

Letter: Accenture’s ‘human error’ claim , a false distinction - Financial Times
Accenture shares dip as earnings report looms
stories.summary: Accenture shares closed at $249.95, a 1.46 percent decline that trailed broader market losses. Despite an 18 percent gain over the past month, the company faces a projected year-over-year earnings decline of 1.0 percent in its upcoming release. Investors remain focused on the firm's financial performance.

stories.title: Accenture ranked among top picks after election
stories.summary: CIBC Capital Markets ranked Accenture 10th on a list of stocks to buy following the Democratic sweep of Congress. The bank designed its stock basket to navigate a potentially tougher regulatory environment for corporate America. The firm remains a target for defensive market strategies.

stories.title: Accenture launches Data-as-a-Service for AI
stories.summary: Accenture has introduced Data-as-a-Service to assist with training, evaluating, and improving AI systems. The offering includes EnterpriseVAL, a tool designed to test large language models against finance and accounting tasks. It serves as a commercial test of the firm's ability to scale AI expertise.

stories.title: McKinsey warns of trade chokepoint risks
stories.summary: McKinsey & Co. reports that the global economy remains vulnerable to disruptions in key shipping passages like the Strait of Hormuz. The analysis frames these chokepoints as a standing liability for corporate earnings, noting that a single blockage can strand components and force factories to cut shifts.

stories.title: A Quarter of Key Goods Vulnerable to Supply Disruptions, Study Finds - WSJ
The Achilles’ heel of global trade: Building resilience where it matters most - McKinsey & Company
Boards urged to measure AI by business outcomes
stories.summary: Boards are evaluating AI success through productivity, return on investment, and business outcomes. While productivity provides an early signal, the firm suggests that long-term enterprise performance is the true measure. Achieving this requires a proven business case and a redesign of how work is performed.

stories.title: KPMG notes disconnect in consulting billing
stories.summary: KPMG's global consulting head says AI has made much traditional advice work nonexistent, yet procurement departments continue to compare bids based on headcount and hourly rates. This practice keeps time-based billing competitive even as clients state they want to pay for outcomes instead of hours.

stories.title: McKinsey Has a New Idea for AI: Teach It How Your CEO Makes Decisions - Inc.com
Banking sector faces AI disruption
stories.summary: Agentic AI may alter banking economics over the next five years by lowering barriers to entry and stripping friction from profitable products. The technology could disrupt competitive moats and customer relationships. The industry is currently evaluating whether AI can build sustainable value beyond simple productivity gains.

stories.title: Bain says banks should use AI to protect profits
stories.summary: Bain & Company argues that AI is more than a productivity tool and can help banks extend market leadership by building winning value propositions. The firm suggests that banks should set competitive strategies first and then deploy AI to support them. The landscape is shifting rapidly.

AI could cut banking industry's cost base by 20% - McKinsey - Banks.am
McKinsey projects healthcare value shift
stories.summary: McKinsey & Company finds healthcare services and technology is the industry's fastest-growing value pool. Total provider EBITDA rebounded to 369 billion dollars in 2025, while payer EBITDA fell to 9 billion dollars. AI is cited as a primary accelerator for these structural changes in revenue generation.

stories.title: Consulting industry faces AI disruption
stories.summary: Technology entrepreneur Jannie van Zyl writes that the management consulting profession is finished. He claims the industry's business model of selling hype and slide-making is being dismantled by the very AI technology its practitioners are currently overhyping. The industry is being asked to provide its own replacement.

stories.title: Deloitte acquires Flipside Crypto AI unit
stories.summary: Deloitte has acquired the AI business of Flipside Crypto and launched a new enterprise AI company called Edisyl. The 24-person operating team from Flipside, including CEO Dave Balter, will staff the new venture. Edisyl focuses on building the knowledge layer for enterprise AI applications.

stories.title: KPMG in India opens sports technology hub
stories.summary: KPMG in India has launched a Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru to help sports organisations accelerate digital transformation. The initiative aims to address operational challenges using emerging technologies and industry expertise. The hub was opened by KPMG India CEO Yezdi Nagporewalla and Indian Olympic Association President P.T. Usha.

stories.title: KPMG launches Sports Tech Hub in Bengaluru, eyes $40-billion Indian sports industry by 2030 - Moneycontrol.com
KPMG targets India sports market growth
stories.summary: KPMG has launched a Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru to capitalise on India's sports industry, which is projected to grow from 21 billion dollars to 40 billion dollars by 2030. The facility will focus on AI, data analytics, and digital solutions for athlete performance and fan engagement.

stories.title: KPMG launches sports tech hub in Bengaluru
stories.summary: KPMG has opened a Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru to develop AI, computer vision, and analytics solutions for sporting organisations. The firm aims to tap into India's rising 21 billion dollar sports economy. The facility focuses on areas including talent identification and stadium management.

stories.title: eClerx acquires RegEdge for compliance
stories.summary: eClerx has acquired RegEdge, a consulting firm specialising in financial services risk management and regulatory compliance. The acquisition adds expertise in compliance transformation and transaction reporting to eClerx's existing analytics and business process management services. Financial terms were not disclosed.

stories.title: eClerx to buy RegEdge for 12 million dollars
stories.summary: eClerx Services is acquiring risk and regulatory consulting firm RegEdge for up to 12 million dollars. RegEdge generated 5.1 million dollars in revenue during 2025. The transaction adds regulatory capabilities serving Tier-1 financial institutions across the US, UK, and India.

stories.title: eClerx announces RegEdge acquisition
stories.summary: eClerx Services will acquire US-based RegEdge for up to 12 million dollars, including performance-linked payments. The acquisition gives eClerx full ownership of the firm to strengthen its financial services regulatory consulting and compliance capabilities. Shares traded marginally higher following the announcement.

stories.title: AGA acquires Ontario's Aria Benefits in national benefits push - Dealroom
AGA Benefit Solutions buys Aria Benefits
stories.summary: AGA Benefit Solutions has acquired Ontario-based benefits consulting firm Aria Benefits. The move follows AGA's return to entirely Canadian ownership after investors bought out the stake previously held by U.S. private equity firm TA Associates. CEO Martin Papillon indicated further transactions may follow.

stories.title: Deloitte recruits KPMG Australia restructuring team
stories.summary: Deloitte has hired KPMG Australia's national turnaround and restructuring leader Tim Mableson along with two partners and several colleagues. The group previously worked at Ferrier Hodgson before its 2019 acquisition by KPMG. The departures mark a continued loss of senior personnel for the accounting firm.

stories.title: KPMG Pakistan firm leaves global network
stories.summary: KPMG's Pakistani member firm has left the global network to operate independently as Taseer Hadi Khalid and Co. The split follows disagreements over centralised regional management plans. The firm, which joined the network in 1987, will continue to serve its existing clients and staff.

stories.title: NITI Aayog reports on PLI scheme progress
stories.summary: A NITI Aayog report notes that India's PLI schemes have created 849,069 jobs, reaching 28 per cent of the full-tenure target. Advanced chemistry cell battery capacity is at 1.4 GWh against a 50 GWh goal. The government think tank is auditing its own flagship programme.

stories.title: PLI schemes hit investment and production targets but lag on jobs
stories.summary: Niti Aayog reports that India's PLI schemes have reached 76 percent of their investment target and 64 percent of production goals as of March 2026. While the government claims the schemes are generating meaningful additionality, employment figures remain at 28 percent of the full-tenure target.

stories.title: PLI schemes generate Rs 22.66 lakh crore production, but job creation reaches only 28% of target: NITI Aayog
stories.summary: India's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have attracted investments worth Rs 2.40 lakh crore and generated production valued at Rs 22.66 lakh crore as of March 2026, according to a report by NITI Aayog prepared in collaboration with IIM Ahmedabad. stories.title: PLI schemes generate just 28% of targeted jobs, raising questions over manufacturing employment
stories.summary: India’s production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes have delivered only 28 per cent of their targeted employment generation by FY26, despite making considerably better progress in attracting investments. stories.summary: A new NITI Aayog assessment reveals that India's ambitious Production-Linked Incentive schemes have significantly underperformed in job creation, meeting only 28% of their target by FY26, prompting calls for a critical redesign and a strategic shift towards demand-side support. stories.title: Chartered accountancy firms remain active in India
stories.summary: Chartered accountancy firms provide services ranging from statutory audits and taxation to forensic accounting and business restructuring. These firms serve a diverse client base including individuals, startups, multinational corporations, and government agencies. The industry continues to function as a key component of the national financial and regulatory ecosystem.

stories.title: Business consulting sector expands in India
stories.summary: The business consulting sector in India is expanding as organizations seek guidance on strategy, digital transformation, and operational excellence. Firms operating in the country combine global methodologies with local market understanding to support large enterprises, mid-sized companies, and government bodies in a dynamic economic environment.

stories.title: Global capability centers reach 2,117 in India
stories.summary: India hosts 2,117 global capability centers, generating 98.4 billion dollars and employing 2.36 million professionals. While Bengaluru remains the largest hub, Hyderabad is capturing the biggest share of new openings. Companies are shifting these centers from cost savings toward product development, AI work, and global strategy.

stories.title: Audit firms increase pay ahead of rotation
stories.summary: Audit and advisory firms have rolled out 10 to 15 percent pay hikes to retain staff before mandatory auditor rotations. Top performers received up to 28 percent. Firms are now linking future compensation to the use of AI tools. Retention is the current priority.

stories.title: Menzies adopts AI resource management
stories.summary: Menzies has implemented an AI-powered resource management platform to transition from an office-led structure to a service-line-led model across its 11 UK offices. The firm is now managing capacity at a firm-wide level. Larger industry players continue to shed staff, potentially complicating their long-term AI adoption.
